sections.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
sections.abstract: The paper determines the extremal subset-sum function in the regular range and proves arithmetic-dependent asymptotics and non-convergence in the irregular range, including an inverse theorem and Lean-checked cases.
sections.claimed_result: For c≥1, the authors prove f_c(n)=⌊cn⌋−⌈n/2⌉; for 0<c<1, they prove non-convergence, give a limsup and arithmetic-class limits under stated conditions, and establish a density-threshold inverse theorem for subset sums.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f_c(n) is the largest size of a subset of {1,…,⌊cn⌋} avoiding n as a sum of distinct elements. The inverse theorem assumes integer s≥1, q the least positive integer not dividing s, ε>0, sufficiently large T, and 2^(q−2)E≤sT; a set A⊆[1,E] with |A|≥E/q+εT then contains a subset summing to sT.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors leave behavior along classes with least non-divisor outside their eligible set Q(c) open; not all higher-q cases are machine-checked.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors say this resolves Erdős–Graham Problem #361 and give an inverse theorem; the paper reports Lean 4 formalization for principal cases and links an author proof repository. sections.title: Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
sections.abstract: The authors construct noncongruent smooth isometric embeddings of positive-genus closed surfaces in Euclidean 3-space that remain tight and differ only in a compact part of the negatively curved region.
sections.claimed_result: For every genus g≥1, the authors construct a metric admitting uncountably many smooth noncongruent tight isometric embeddings into R³; the embeddings agree outside a compact subset and enclose different volumes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed orientable surfaces of positive genus with a constructed Riemannian metric; embeddings are smooth (C∞) and tight in the stated total-positive-curvature sense.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly leave open whether their examples are flexible, meaning they lie in a continuous one-parameter family of noncongruent isometric embeddings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main theorem gives uncountably many noncongruent embeddings and the authors identify it as settling questions of Nirenberg and Banchoff–Kühnel; the differential-geometry/PDE cross-list is a secondary relevance signal. Semantic Scholar reports 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
sections.abstract: For the 3D focusing energy-critical wave equation, the authors construct a bounded forward-global solution near a sign-changing stationary state whose stationary core has two distinct similarity-orbit limits after subtracting radiation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors disprove the specified full-time resolution assertion with a fixed finite list of stationary profiles and fixed Lorentz velocities by constructing a bounded forward-global solution with subsequences approaching stationary states in distinct similarity orbits.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The equation is the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical quintic wave equation; the constructed solution is forward-global, bounded in the energy space, and starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state.
sections.unique_caveat: The result targets the fixed-profile quantifier order; it does not rule out sequential decompositions in which profiles may be chosen for a particular time sequence. The certificate is computationally assisted and remains part of an unreviewed preprint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Theorem 1.1 is a concrete counterexample to a precise fixed-profile assertion, and the authors include a computer-assisted certificate for the stationary state and its odd energy kernel. Semantic Scholar reports 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: On L^p density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
sections.abstract: The authors show that every absolutely continuous self-similar measure in their setting has an L^p density for some p>1 and establish explicit Bernoulli convolutions with continuous densities.
sections.claimed_result: For a probability measure supported on finitely many contracting similarities of R^d, absolute continuity of its self-similar measure implies its density belongs to L^p(R^d) for some p>1; the paper also gives explicit Bernoulli-convolution examples with continuous density.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The general theorem assumes finitely many contracting similarities and an absolutely continuous associated self-similar probability measure. Bernoulli-convolution examples use additional parameter conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The general result promises some p>1, not a universal exponent; the explicit continuous-density examples cover a restricted parameter range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result links dynamical systems, analysis, and probability; the authors state that the new results are formalized in Lean. Semantic Scholar reports 0 current citations and 0 influential citations.

sections.title: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
sections.abstract: The author proves that every mod-2 Galois representation of a global field lifts mod 4, constructs non-liftable examples for every odd prime at the next prime-power level, and completes a classification of liftable finite groups.
sections.claimed_result: All mod-2 Galois representations of a global field lift modulo 4; for each odd prime p, the author gives global-field representations mod p that do not lift mod p², and proves liftability of generalized quaternion groups.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Galois representations of global fields with the stated mod-2/mod-4 or mod-p/mod-p² coefficient levels; the group-classification consequence concerns liftable finite groups.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s positive and negative results concern these specific adjacent coefficient levels; it does not assert a general lifting criterion at all powers or for all coefficient rings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract combines a uniform mod-2 lifting theorem, counterexamples at every odd prime, and a stated completion of a finite-group classification. sections.title: On the maximum of Poissonian log-correlated fields
sections.abstract: For a stationary log-correlated field built from a Poisson sequence of random frequencies and uniform phases, the authors obtain a high-probability maximum asymptotic with a random-time fluctuation and logarithmic correction.
sections.claimed_result: For centered analytic 1-periodic f and the stated rate-1 Poisson arrival-time/uniform-phase model, the authors prove with high probability max X_n=c₁n+c₂τ_n−(c₃+o(1))log n, with positive constants depending on f.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The field is the sum of f(e^{τ_j}t+v_j) over the first n points, where τ_j are rate-1 Poisson arrival times and v_j are iid uniform on [0,1); f is centered, analytic, and 1-periodic.
sections.unique_caveat: The analogous asymptotics for characteristic polynomials of random permutation matrices and sparse random matrices are conjectured/expected by the authors, not proved here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper states an explicit three-term maximum asymptotic and connects its proof to branching random walks in a random time environment. sections.title: Dimension drop for superlevel sets of the uniform Littlewood constant
sections.abstract: Although the set where the uniform Littlewood constant is positive has full Hausdorff dimension, the authors prove every fixed positive superlevel set has dimension strictly below two and polynomially decaying finite-scale measure.
sections.claimed_result: For every fixed c>0, the set {L≥c} has Hausdorff dimension strictly less than two, and the measure of {(x,y)∈[0,1]²:F_Q(x,y)≥c} is O_c(Q^−κ(c)) for some κ(c)>0 and all Q≥2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: F_Q(x,y)=Q min_{1≤q≤Q}||qx||||qy|| and L=limsup_{Q→∞}F_Q; the result is for each fixed positive threshold c.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives no explicit value for κ(c) or exact dimension of the superlevel set; its strict upper bound is not a complete dimension classification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper bridges Diophantine approximation and homogeneous dynamics, giving both a Hausdorff-dimension drop and a quantitative measure bound.
